newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil trade dulled by IPE expiry volatilty.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil trade dulled by IPE expiry volatilty.

text.p: NWE gas oil outright prices fluctuated wildly as benchmark gas oil futures were hit by bouts of long liquidation and short-covering on Thursday ahead of expiry at noon, traders said.
Barge and cargo prices for heating oil and diesel moved up by almost $2 a tonne in early business as July gas oil futures rose on short-covering and premiums strengthened slightly.

But long liquidation as traders rolled positions forward into August wiped out all of the early gains before a further bout of short-covering before the expiry pushed them back to around unchanged levels.
Brokers said the futures volatility kept most physical buyers out of the market though the 75 cents to $1 contango to August saw sellers keeping offers high.

Prompt heating oil liftings were offered at July IPE +$2 fob Rotterdam, 50 cents higher than on Wednesday with tight supplies also underpinning premiums. Second half July contracts talked August IPE + 50 cents to +$2 a tonne fob ARA.
Prompt diesel barges talked Aug IPE +$4/$5 a tonne fob ARA.
0.2 sulphur cargoes were pegged around August IPE +$2 after trade into Germany either side of the level on Wednesday.
Diesel cargoes talked August IPE +$3.50/$4.50 cif NWE.
